stem.text: 2-bromomethylpropane is heated with concentrated NaOH in ethanol under reflux.
Which statement about the major product of this reaction is correct?

options.text: Methylpropene is produced in an elimination reaction.
Methylpropene is produced in a condensation reaction.
Methylpropan-2-ol is produced in an S<sub>N</sub>1 reaction.
Methylpropan-2-ol is produced in an S<sub>N</sub>2 reaction.

explanation.text: The solvent decides the main reaction of a halogenoalkane with NaOH. In ethanol, OH<sup>–</sup> acts mainly as a base, removing H and Br from neighbouring carbons (elimination of HBr) to give an alkene. In water, OH<sup>–</sup> acts as a nucleophile and substitution gives an alcohol.

2-bromomethylpropane, (CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>3</sub>CBr, is tertiary, so any substitution would go by S<sub>N</sub>1; but under these ethanolic conditions the major product is methylpropene, (CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>C=CH<sub>2</sub>.

optionAnalysis.text: NaOH in ethanol with heat eliminates HBr from (CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>3</sub>CBr, giving methylpropene.
The product is right, but losing HBr from one molecule is elimination; condensation joins two molecules with loss of a small molecule.
S<sub>N</sub>1 to methylpropan-2-ol is what a tertiary bromide does with aqueous NaOH, not with NaOH in ethanol.
Tertiary halogenoalkanes do not react by S<sub>N</sub>2 (the carbon is too hindered), and ethanolic NaOH favours elimination anyway.

reasoningChain: Conditions: concentrated NaOH in ethanol, reflux = elimination conditions.
The reaction type is elimination: option A.

inferredMistakes.text: Spotting that the halogenoalkane is tertiary and choosing S<sub>N</sub>1, without noticing that the solvent is ethanol rather than water.
